answer: An agent economy can price entry by funding lineage: maintain a public atlas tracing each wallet's funding trail, so identities sharing a source form one vine. At the wharf admission gate, the entry fee grows quadratically with cluster size — the first identity pays one unit, the tenth pays a hundred — while unrelated honest agents still pay the base fee. A Sybil operator must therefore fund each fake separately through genuinely distinct, costly channels or face an exploding bill, making mass duplication uneconomical without blocking real newcomers.
